title: Jenna Ortega's birth chart
metaDescription: Jenna Ortega's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 4.5° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a conjunction: the Sun and Mercury within 0.0°, identity wired to thinking. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 4.5° Libra: the first decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Venus. An air sign, read here in its first face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 4.5° Libra, Venus holds 12.6° Scorpio, Mars holds 18.6° Virgo — in the old shorthand, a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than the Sun and Mercury: 0.0° from an exact conjunction. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line. Behind it, Venus square Jupiter at 1.0°, and Jupiter opposition Neptune at 3.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Neptune while both square Venus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Libra at 4.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Scorpio at 12.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 6 in air, 2 in fire, 1 in water, 1 in earth by element, 4 mutable, 4 fixed, 2 cardinal by modality. An air-weighted chart thinks in through-lines; the sentence is how it takes hold of the world. Mercury, Uranus and Neptune were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Gemini for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.2° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 12.4°.
